subject: Maths
title: Conditional probability and Venn diagrams
subtitle: Probability · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can use Venn diagrams to find probabilities including conditional probability.

key_vocab.definition: Conditional probability is the probability of an event given that another event has already occurred. Venn diagrams help us visualise overlapping groups.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can use Venn diagrams to find probabilities including conditional probability.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Conditional probability -- Conditional probability is the probability of an event given that another event has already occurred. Venn diagrams help us visualise overlapping groups.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
In a Venn diagram, the overlap shows items in BOTH sets. Conditional probability restricts to a subset.
P(A|B) = &frac{n(A∩B)}{n(B)}
Given B, only look at members of B

Key examples:
  ✓ P(A|B) = P(A∩B) ÷ P(B)  (conditional formula)
  ✓ A Venn diagram shows overlapping sets  (intersection)
  ✓ P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A∩B)  (addition rule)
  ✗ P(A|B) = P(A) always  (only if independent)
  ✗ P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B)  (must subtract overlap)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – reading a Venn diagram
  In a class of 30: 18 like football, 12 like tennis, 5 like both. Find P(football only).
  Football only = 18 - 5 = 13
  Total = 30
  P(football only) = &frac{13}{30}
  = &frac{13}{30}
  (Subtract the overlap to find the football-only region.)

Example 2 – conditional probability
  Using the same data: find P(tennis | likes football).
  Given they like football: 18 students
  Of these, 5 also like tennis
  P(tennis|football) = &frac{5}{18}
  = &frac{5}{18}
  (Restrict to the football group, then find those who also like tennis.)

sections.title: Reading Venn diagrams
sections.content:
A class of 40: A = 22, B = 18, A∩B = 8, neither = 8. Find:

(a) P(A only)
(b) P(B only)
(c) P(A∪B)
(d) P(neither)

sections.title: Conditional probability
sections.content:
Using: A = 22, B = 18, A∩B = 8, total = 40.

(a) P(B|A)
(b) P(A|B)
(c) P(not B|A)
(d) P(A|not B)

sections.title: Completing Venn diagrams
sections.content:
Find the missing values.

(a) Total 50, A = 30, B = 20, A∩B = 7. Neither?
(b) Total 80, A = 45, B = 35, neither = 15. A∩B?
(c) Total 100, A only = 25, B only = 30, neither = 20. A∩B?
(d) Total 60, A = 40, A∩B = 12, neither = 5. B?

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
Draw a Venn diagram and find the probability.

(a) 50 people: 30 drink tea, 25 drink coffee, 15 drink both. P(tea only)?
(b) Same data: P(coffee | drinks tea)?
(c) Same data: P(neither)?
(d) Same data: P(tea | drinks coffee)?

sections.title: Mixed conditional probability
sections.content:
Use the given information.

(a) P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5, P(A∩B) = 0.3. Find P(A∪B)
(b) Same: find P(A|B)
(c) Same: find P(B|A)
(d) Are A and B independent? Explain
(e) P(neither A nor B)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ P(A|B) means restrict to set B then find P(A)
✗ P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) always
✓ If P(A|B) = P(A) then A and B are independent
✗ P(A|B) is the same as P(B|A)
✓ P(A∪B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A∩B)
